# Fork & upstream sync

Dev Island is a fork of [Octane0411/open-vibe-island](https://github.com/Octane0411/open-vibe-island)
(GPL v3) that **keeps syncing from upstream** while carrying a **full rename** of the product.

Those two goals fight each other: the rename touches nearly every file, so a naive merge would
conflict on almost every upstream commit. This document is the working agreement that makes the
combination survivable.

## The rule

**The rename is never resolved by hand. It is regenerated by `scripts/rebrand.sh`, which is
idempotent.** So the answer to any rename conflict is always the same: take upstream's version of
the file wholesale, then re-run the script.

That leaves a short, enumerable list of files the script cannot regenerate because they contain
fork-specific decisions rather than a mechanical rename. **These are the only files that need human
judgement on a sync:**

| File | Why it is hand-maintained |
|---|---|
| `README.md`, `README.zh-CN.md` | Fork attribution, no Homebrew cask, no fork-owned community channels |
| `appcast.xml` | Reset to an empty feed, not rebranded |
| `scripts/package-app.sh` | Sparkle keys emitted conditionally instead of hardcoded |
| `.github/workflows/release.yml` | Homebrew tap step disabled |
| `scripts/rebrand.sh`, `docs/fork-sync.md` | They *are* the rebrand |

## Syncing

```bash
git fetch upstream
git merge -X theirs upstream/main    # rename conflicts resolve in upstream's favour

# Regenerate the rename over the merged tree.
bash scripts/rebrand.sh

# `-X theirs` will have reverted the hand-maintained files above to upstream's version.
# Restore them, and re-apply the fork's edits to any that upstream actually changed:
git checkout HEAD -- README.md README.zh-CN.md appcast.xml
git diff upstream/main -- scripts/package-app.sh .github/workflows/release.yml

swift build && swift test
git commit -am "chore: merge upstream vX.Y.Z and regenerate rebrand"
```

`bash scripts/rebrand.sh --check` is a dry run: it reports what would change and exits non-zero if
anything still carries upstream branding. Useful as a CI guard, and as the last thing to run before
committing a sync.

> **Do not** try to keep the rebrand as a separate commit and drop it with
> `git rebase --onto upstream/main <rebrand> main`. Anything the fork changed *before* that commit
> is silently discarded, and putting the rebrand at the tip leaves nothing for the rebase to replay.
> The merge-and-regenerate flow above needs no commit topology at all, which is why it is the one
> documented here.

## What the script does

Two passes over `git ls-files`, most-specific rule first so no rule shadows another:

| From | To |
|---|---|
| `Octane0411/open-vibe-island` | `vincentlauriat/dev-island` |
| `open-vibe-island` | `dev-island` |
| `OPEN_ISLAND` | `DEV_ISLAND` |
| `OpenIsland` | `DevIsland` |
| `Open Island` | `Dev Island` |
| `openisland` | `devisland` |
| `open-island` | `dev-island` |

Paths are renamed file by file (not directory by directory) so nested cases like
`ios/OpenIslandMobile.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` resolve in one sweep. Binaries are skipped.

`OpenCode`, `com.openai.*` and the legacy `VIBE_ISLAND_SOCKET_PATH` env var match no rule and are
left alone on purpose.

### Files the script must never touch

Same list as the hand-maintained table above. Two of them are excluded for a reason worth spelling
out: `scripts/rebrand.sh` and this document *contain* the substitution rules, so rewriting them
would collapse every rule into a no-op and silently break idempotence.

## Runtime identity

The rename moves the user-visible runtime surface. This is deliberate: it is what lets Dev Island
and Open Island run side by side on one machine.

| | Upstream | This fork |
|---|---|---|
| Socket dir | `~/Library/Application Support/OpenIsland/` | `.../DevIsland/` |
| Legacy socket | `/tmp/open-island-$UID.sock` | `/tmp/dev-island-$UID.sock` |
| Codex state | `~/Library/Application Support/open-island` | `.../dev-island` |
| Bundle id | `app.openisland.OpenIsland` | `app.devisland.DevIsland` |
| Socket env var | `OPEN_ISLAND_SOCKET_PATH` | `DEV_ISLAND_SOCKET_PATH` |

**Consequence**: hooks installed by Open Island keep pointing at the old socket. Dev Island installs
its own from its Settings window. This is intended, not a regression.

## Release chain

Three wires into upstream infrastructure had to be cut, and must stay cut:

- **`SUFeedURL`** now points at this fork's `appcast.xml`. Left at upstream's, a Dev Island user
  would be auto-updated back onto Open Island.
- **`SUPublicEDKey`** is no longer hardcoded. `scripts/package-app.sh` emits the Sparkle keys only
  when `DEV_ISLAND_EDDSA_PUBLIC_KEY` is set; with it unset, Sparkle fails to start and
  `UpdateChecker` catches it, so the app simply runs without auto-update. Upstream's public key was
  removed rather than kept: its private half lives with upstream, so it could neither sign this
  fork's builds nor validate anything served from here.
- **`appcast.xml`** was reset to an empty feed. Its 48 entries pointed at upstream DMGs and carried
  upstream EdDSA signatures.
- **The Homebrew tap job** in `.github/workflows/release.yml` is `if: false`. It opened and
  self-merged a PR against `Octane0411/homebrew-tap`, which is upstream's tap.

### Before the first release

1. Generate a keypair with Sparkle's `generate_keys`.
2. Public half → `DEV_ISLAND_EDDSA_PUBLIC_KEY` at package time.
3. Private half → `SPARKLE_EDDSA_KEY` repository secret.
4. Sign under `Developer ID Application: Vincent LAURIAT (KFLACS69T9)`, notarize with the
   `AppliMacVincentGithub` keychain profile.

## The dev app

`scripts/launch-dev-app.sh` now builds `~/Applications/Dev Island Dev.app` under bundle id
`app.devisland.dev`. macOS keys TCC grants to the bundle id, so **Accessibility and Automation
permissions granted to Open Island's dev app do not carry over**. Before using any AX-touching
feature (precision jump, keystroke/menu injection):

```bash
zsh scripts/setup-dev-signing.sh   # once, or every rebuild silently invalidates the grants
zsh scripts/launch-dev-app.sh
```

Then re-approve the prompts in System Settings → Privacy & Security.

## Known gaps

- **Visual identity**: icons are upstream's artwork, renamed. `scripts/generate_brand_icons.py` and
  `scripts/generate-v6-appicon.swift` are the path to a real Dev Island icon set. Same for
  `docs/images/readme-banner.svg` and `docs/images/demo.gif`, whose *text* was rebranded but whose
  artwork is still upstream's.
- **`ios/`** is a separate Xcode project outside the SwiftPM package. It is not covered by
  `swift build` / `swift test`, so its rename is verified by inspection only.
